chunk_findings.detail: `_is_trivial` delegates to `diff_is_trivial(it, cfg, repo, changed_paths(repo, it))`, but `changed_paths(repo, it)` is the committed-diff path list and does not include untracked files in the dirty tree under test. A tree whose tracked diff is docs-only, but which also contains an untracked `new_feature.py` with real code changes, will be classified as trivial: the new logic file is not among the paths passed to `diff_is_trivial`, so `_selectable` returns `"a trivial change (...)"` and the full suite is skipped, leaving that code untested. The earlier fail-closed dirty-tree fix only covers tracked paths, not untracked ones.

chunk_findings.detail: `_is_trivial` classifies the item with `W.repo_root(tree)` and then `diff_is_trivial`, whose dirty-tree and AST checks use that repo's `HEAD` (the same `git diff HEAD` path the prior `[a].py` fix describes). In a linked worktree, `HEAD` is the main checkout, not `tree`. Given main clean at base with `foo.py` as `x = 1`, and the item worktree holding a format-only commit plus an uncommitted `x = 1` → `x = 2` in `foo.py`, `changed_paths` still lists `foo.py`, the dirty check against main is empty, and the change is treated as trivial, so `_selectable` returns a scoped run for a logic edit. Pass `tree` (the tree under test) into `diff_is_trivial`, not the main worktree.

chunk_findings.detail: `_py_ast_equal` compares only `ast.dump(ast.parse(...))`, which erases concrete syntax beyond whitespace/comments. For example a committed diff from `x = 1` to `x = 0x1` (or `x = "a" "b"` to `x = "ab"`) changes the code, but both sides dump as the same `Constant(value=1)`/`Constant(value='ab')`. `_ast_unchanged` then returns True, `_is_format_or_comment` calls it format-only/comment-only, and `diff_is_trivial` drops `rubber_duck`, `critic`, and `ci`, even though the diff edits code and is outside the allowed format/comment classes. That violates the gate contract that a logic/code change is never trivial.

chunk_findings.detail: The “uncommitted edits fail closed” check is scoped to the `paths` argument (`git diff HEAD -- :(literal)<path>`). A worktree whose committed diff is a comment-only edit to `foo.py` (`paths == ["foo.py"]`) but which also has an **uncommitted** tracked logic edit to `bar.py` (`x = 1` -> `x = 2`) is not detected: the diff command for `foo.py` is empty and `_ast_unchanged` compares only `foo.py`, so `_is_format_or_comment` returns True. `diff_is_trivial` then marks a dirty tree containing a logic change as trivial, skipping review and full CI. The whole-tree dirty status, or a diff check not restricted to `paths`, is required.

chunk_findings.detail: The new trivial path calls `diff_is_trivial(item, cfg, repo, paths)` with the path list produced by the `diff` callable. In `pipeline_diff.py`, that callable is `lambda: changed_paths(repo, item)`, and `changed_paths` excludes untracked files from the dirty tree under test. So a worktree whose tracked diff is only a format-only change to `foo.py`, but which also contains an untracked `feature.py` with real logic changes, has `paths == ["foo.py"]`; `diff_is_trivial` sees only the format-only `foo.py` and returns true, so `pipeline_by_diff` selects `_trivial_pipeline(gates)` and skips full cross-family review and whole-suite CI even though behavior-changing code is present. chunk_findings.detail:
An index-only staged logic edit to a path inside the committed trivial path list is invisible. `_uncommitted_not_in` deliberately permits dirty tracked files whose name is in `paths`, and `_is_format_or_comment` only runs `git diff HEAD -- :(literal)<path>`, which compares the worktree to HEAD and ignores the index. Concrete failure: base `foo.py` is `x = 1
`; HEAD changes it to `x=1
` (AST-equal/format-only), so `paths=["foo.py"]`. Now stage `foo.py` as `x = 2
` and then `git restore --source=HEAD --worktree -- foo.py`. `_uncommitted_not_in` sees `git diff HEAD --cached --name-only` output `foo.py`, but `foo.py in paths`, so it returns False. `_is_format_or_comment` sees an empty worktree-vs-HEAD diff and `_ast_unchanged` compares base vs HEAD (the format-only committed change), so `diff_is_trivial` returns True and skips `rubber_duck`, `critic`, and `ci`, even though a logic change is staged.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/docsonly.py:_is_format_or_comment

chunk_findings.detail: When the uncommitted-work guard fires (`tree is not None and _uncommitted_not_in(...)`), this function returns full `gates`, but it still returns `lambda: paths`, where `paths` is only the original committed `diff()` result. `ddflow/services/gates/outcomes.py` later passes that same diff callable to `not_applicable`. In the exact case the guard exists for — committed diff is `README.md` and there is a dirty tracked `src/module.py` — `paths` remains `["README.md"]`, so any full-pipeline gate whose `applies_when` requires a Python path is marked not applicable and skipped. The guard therefore does not actually produce the full effective pipeline for the uncommitted dirty file; it should include the uncommitted paths in the returned diff when it forces `gates`.

chunk_findings.detail: The new call `diff_is_trivial(it, cfg, repo, changed_paths(repo, it))` passes `cfg` in the position meant for the changed path list. The regression test pins `diff_is_trivial` as receiving the item and the path list as the first two arguments (`diff_is_trivial(None, docs_paths) == True`), with `cfg`/`repo` as the later context arguments. For a behavior-preserving docs-only change where `changed_paths(repo, it)` is `["README.md"]`, this call hands the config object to `diff_is_docs_only` instead of `["README.md"]`, so `diff_is_trivial` returns False; `_is_trivial` then returns False, and a large README-only diff falls through to `_selectable`'s size logic and still runs the whole suite instead of the new trivial scoped tier.

chunk_findings.detail: A behavior change staged only in the index, on a path already in the committed diff, is still classified trivial. `_uncommitted_not_in` only fails closed when a dirty path is absent from `paths`, and `_is_format_or_comment` only runs `git diff HEAD` (worktree vs HEAD), not `git diff HEAD --cached`. Concrete case: commit a whitespace-only edit to `foo.py` (AST equal to base), then change `x = 1` to `x = 2`, `git add foo.py`, and `git restore --source=HEAD --worktree foo.py`.
